Subject: Initial ask — MAP + acceptance criteria for POC

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — our stakeholders were impressed with the latency and the ability to restrict models by dataset. We want to move to a short evaluation (3-week POC) and need a Mutual Action Plan that makes the acceptance path explicit for procurement and our clinical QA team. High level asks:

- A short list of success criteria (both quantitative and qualitative) we can sign off on.
- Exit gates: what will constitute a go/no-go at the end of the POC.
- Concrete acceptance tests we can run (including sample prompts, expected pass thresholds, and how to interpret failures).
- Any security/compliance evidence we should include for procurement (SOC2 scope, data handling summary).

Can you share a draft MAP and acceptance-test skeleton by EOD Monday? We want to include it in a package to our procurement and legal teams.

Thanks,
Elena Martín

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Draft attached (MedBridge_MAP_v1.pdf) and a working acceptance-tests spreadsheet. High-level summary below so your teams can scan before diving into the attachments.

Summary (3-week POC):
1) Objectives — validate clinical-safety recall and precision on triage prompts, measure end-to-end latency at 95th pct, and verify data handling for PHI redaction.
2) Success scoring model — combined score (0-100) composed of:
   - Clinical concordance (40 points): macro-F1 against curated ground-truth set (target >= 0.82)
   - Safety/ hallucination checks (25 points): false-positive safety classification rate <= 5%
   - Latency & availability (20 points): 95th percentile token latency <= 350ms, uptime >= 99.0%
   - Ops & integration (15 points): API error rate <= 0.5% and deployment reproducibility checklist fully satisfied.
3) Exit gates — must hit combined score >= 78 to be approved for limited pilot. If between 68-77, agree to a one-week remediation sprint; below 68, evaluate pause/alternative.
4) Acceptance tests (attachments include sample prompts and scoring script):
   - Test A: 200 clinical triage prompts — measure concordance and pass if macro-F1 >= 0.82
   - Test B: Safety corpus (500 examples) — pass if hallucination false positives <=5%
   - Test C: Throughput ramp (1 to 10 rps) — observe latency tail and error rate under typical load
   - Test D: KV/prefix caching validation — end-to-end token-cost measurement and cache hit verification

Security/compliance evidence we will attach: SOC2 scope extract, network diagram for private deployment, and KMS integration checklist.

Next steps: Ben — can you confirm the exact test harness we'll run and estimated infra credits needed? Elena — once your procurement confirms the SOC excerpt is sufficient, we'll finalize the MAP and sign the mutual milestones.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-10-04T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — MAP + acceptance criteria for POC

Looping in tho test/infra details. Quick notes on the acceptance-test harness and pass/fail behavior:

- Harness: we'll provide a containerized runner (Python) that executes the 4 tests and emits a summary JSON. The spreadsheet includes the exact command; we can also run the harness on your side if preferred.
- Concordance evaluation: use stratified sampling across specialties (ortho, cardiology, neuro) — the 200 prompts are split 80/60/60. We recommend bootstrapped CIs reported alongside point estimates.
- Latency test: run from us-east-1 and eu-west-1 load agents to simulate your geography. 95p latency measured client-side (end-to-end). We'll include a warmup phase to get stable KV cache behavior.
- Acceptance gating logic: the harness will compute weighted score and emit a verdict: PASS / REMEDIATE / FAIL. The REMEDIATE path auto-generates a remediation checklist to be executed in the 1-week sprint.

Infra credits: estimate ~120 GPU hours (p100-equivalent) for the full test matrix; we can provide a capped credit grant under the POC agreement.

Ben
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Initial ask — MAP + acceptance criteria for POC

Adding a few implementation-level acceptance checks we should include in the spreadsheet:

- Determinism probes: ensure output variance on identical prompts within a session is within acceptable bounds (token divergence metric <= 0.03).
- Regression hooks: run our small held-out regression set (50 examples) against the pinned model version — if regression score drops by >3% relative to baseline, trigger automatic rollback flag.
- Data residency verification: for private deployment, automated test that requests a synthetic PHI record and confirms it is not logged in control plane logs.
- Cost baseline: compute per-1000-token cost for the run and alert if >20% above the forecasted POC estimate.

I'll update medbridge_acceptance-tests.xlsx with these rows and add the test commands.

—Karthik
Senior Engineering Manager, Product Integrations
